title: JRE 2298 - Kurt Metzger
guestBio: Kurt Metzger is a stand-up comic, writer, and host of the "Can't Get Right with Kurt Metzger" podcast. His latest special, "30 Minutes with Kurt Metzger," is available on YouTube.
tldr: Kurt Metzger discusses his comedy career and the evolution of stand-up in the modern era
Conversation explores the challenges comedians face with cancel culture and social media
Kurt talks about his podcast Can't Get Right and the creative freedom it provides
Discussion touches on the state of comedy specials and streaming platforms
Kurt shares insights about writing comedy and what makes jokes work
Joe and Kurt discuss the comedy community and relationships between comedians
recap:
Joe brings on stand-up comic Kurt Metzger for a wide-ranging conversation about comedy, the industry, and the current state of entertainment. Kurt is a veteran of the stand-up circuit with his own podcast Can't Get Right with Kurt Metzger, and he's recently released a special titled 30 Minutes with Kurt Metzger on YouTube.

The two dive into how comedy has changed over the years, with a focus on how social media and the internet have transformed the landscape for comedians. Kurt talks about the balance between pushing boundaries in comedy and navigating the sensitivities of modern audiences. They discuss the creative freedom that comes with platforms like YouTube and podcasting versus traditional media, which often comes with more restrictions and corporate oversight.

Kurt shares his perspective on what makes comedy work and how he approaches writing material. The conversation touches on the relationships between comedians, the community aspect of the comedy world, and how comedians support each other. They also explore the topic of how specials are consumed now versus how they were in the past, with streaming platforms changing the game entirely.

Throughout the episode, Joe and Kurt keep the energy light and conversational, with plenty of laughs as they discuss the absurdities of the entertainment industry and the comedy world specifically. Kurt brings his perspective as someone who's been grinding in comedy for years and has seen the industry transform multiple times. The discussion feels authentic to the JRE format, with tangents and real talk about what it takes to be a working comedian in today's world.
